entry.title: Note that Safari 27 disables `display` transitions for popovers and `<dialog>`
entry.content:
Summary

Adds a Safari note to css.properties.display.is_animatable: since Safari 27, display transitions are disabled for popovers and <dialog> elements. Support stays at 18 with no partial_implementation, as suggested in the issue, since WebKit disabled this on purpose while the spec questions are open. Safari on iOS inherits the note through mirror.

Test results and supporting details

WebKit bug 311648, "Disable display property transitions for popover & ", is resolved fixed by 310725@main on 2026-04-07, with the test LayoutTests/transitions/no-display-transition-top-layer.html. The commit cites w3c/csswg-drafts#13595 and w3c/csswg-drafts#13200. It landed while WebKit was at 625.1.14, which puts it in Safari 27 (625.1.29); Safari 26.6 shipped 624.4.5 and does not have it.

entry.title: devtools.panels Safari support corrections
entry.content:
Summary

#20403 set Safari to 16 for these features. Safari 16's release notes do announce Web Inspector Extensions, but no Apple source names any of these APIs. Safari's extension APIs are defined in WebKit's IDL files, and none of these features appear there. Apple's documentation doesn't mention any of them either.

Test results and supporting details

devtools.panels: Button, ExtensionPanel.createStatusBarButton, openResource, setOpenResourceHandler, sources

  • WebExtensionAPIDevToolsPanels.idl L29–36: devtools.panels defines only create(), themeName and onThemeChanged. It has no openResource(), setOpenResourceHandler(), sources or Button.
  • WebExtensionAPIDevToolsExtensionPanel.idl L29–34: ExtensionPanel defines only onShown and onHidden. It has no createStatusBarButton(), so Safari can't create a Button object.
  • A search of the WebKit repository finds no createStatusBarButton and no Button interface for devtools extensions.
  • WebInspectorExtensionController.js: Web Inspector's extension controller handles extension tabs (create, navigate, show, hide, evaluate script, reload). It has nothing for opening resources, a sources panel or status bar buttons.

devtools.inspectedWindow: Resource (and its getContent, setContent, url), getResources, onResourceAdded, onResourceContentCommitted

  • WebExtensionAPIDevToolsInspectedWindow.idl L37–44: inspectedWindow defines only eval(), reload() and tabId. It has no Resource type, no getResources() and no resource events.

devtools.inspectedWindow.eval() option scriptExecutionContext

  • WebExtensionAPIDevToolsInspectedWindow.idl L26–28: the eval options dictionary declares only frameURL.
  • WebExtensionAPIDevToolsInspectedWindowCocoa.mm L48–56: the implementation accepts only frameURLKey. Other options are ignored. The same applies to contextSecurityOrigin and useContentScriptContext, which #31154 corrects.

Apple sources checked (none mention any of these features):

  • Safari release notes for 15.4, 16.0–16.5, 17.0 and 18.0. Safari 16.0 says only "Added support for Safari Web Inspector Extensions."
  • WebKit features in Safari 16.0
  • WWDC22 session 10100, "Create Safari Web Inspector Extensions". It names only devtools.panels.create, devtools.inspectedWindow.eval (with frameURL), devtools.network.onNavigated and the theme APIs.
  • Adding a web development tool to Safari Web Inspector
  • Assessing your Safari web extension's browser compatibility

entry.title: Merge -webkit-hyphenate-limit-lines into hyphenate-limit-lines
entry.content: WebKit treats -webkit-hyphenate-limit-lines as an alias of the unprefixed hyphenate-limit-lines property, so record it as a -webkit- prefix on hyphenate-limit-lines instead of a separate entry. It's also more helpful to have those as a combined entry so they both appear on the relevant MDN page later.

entry.title: Add `Content-Encoding: gzip`
entry.content:
Summary

Adds a gzip row to http.headers.Content-Encoding, next to br, dcb, dcz and zstd. Its data is the same as the Content-Encoding row itself.

I left deflate and compress out. IE only accepted raw deflate streams without the zlib wrapper, so deflate would need notes. compress doesn't work in any major browser.

Test results and supporting details

npm test passes. After npm run build, the resolved gzip support equals the parent row's.

Sources:

  • Chrome 1: Chromium's first public commit already decodes gzip and x-gzip (net/base/filter.cc).
  • Firefox 1: Gecko's HTTP compression converter handled gzip before Firefox 1.0 (nsHTTPCompressConv.cpp, June 2004), and the default network.http.accept-encoding was already gzip,deflate (all.js, October 2004).
  • Safari 1: WebKit loads through NSURLConnection, which came with Safari 1.0, and NSURLConnection decodes gzip and deflate (WebKit bug 4648, comment 6).
  • IE: decoded gzip in URLMon up to IE 6 and in WinINET from IE 7 (Compressing the Web, IEInternals). I kept the parent's ≤11.
  • Edge 12: Edge's first release, same as the parent row. Those first versions came from #23725, which covers headers in the HTTP/1.1 spec. gzip is a content coding in that same spec (RFC 2616 section 3.5).

Related issues

Fixes #31171

entry.title: Firefox supports WebGPU in service workers from 148
entry.content:
Summary

Firefox supports WebGPU in service workers from version 148. Remove the note about the service worker restriction everywhere it appears. I have not replaced it with a note stating that support started in 148, to me that doesn't seem like an important enough point to be worth cluttering all of these pages with the note. But I can add it if desired.

There were two instances of the alternate note text "Supported on Windows only, in all contexts except for service workers." One of these was GPUDevice.importExternalTexture, where that note was correct when added, but is no longer correct. I removed it and replaced it with the full standard set of WebGPU notes (but support starts in Firefox 144, not Firefox 141).

The other instance was in the data for the GPUPipelineError message parameter being optional. I am not aware of any reason this differs from the rest of the WebGPU items, so I replaced it with the standard set of WebGPU notes.

I also deleted "Supported on Windows only, in all contexts except for service workers." from the OS_NOTES list in scripts/build/mirror.js.

entry.title: Safari 26.4 changes devicePixelRatio on page zoom
entry.content:
Summary

Safari 26.4 fixed devicePixelRatio so that page zoom changes it for the main frame. The data still marks every Safari version as partial with the "does not change when the page is zoomed" note, so this adds a full support statement for 26.4 and keeps the note for Safari 3 to 26.3.

Test results and supporting details

The Safari 26.4 release notes include "Fixed devicePixelRatio so that page zoom now affects the main frame consistently with iframes, keeping their values synchronized. (163857955)". That radar is WebKit/WebKit@bdfffc7361a6 (303397@main, bug 301807), which changes LocalFrame::frameScaleFactor() so page zoom applies to the main frame too. WebKit trunk was at 624.1.4 when it landed, Safari 26.3 shipped 623.2.7 and Safari 26.4 shipped 624.1.16.

A comment on bug 124862 reports the value changing with zoom in Safari 26.5, and #31039 has the same result in Safari 27.2.

Zooming still doesn't fire change on a (resolution: <n>dppx) media query (bug 317839), so the monitoring example on the MDN page doesn't work in Safari. That's about the media query rather than this property, so I left it out here.

entry.title: Add MathML and SVG drawable attribute, and DOM property equivalents
entry.content:
Summary

Chrome 157 adds support for the HTML-in-Canvas API; see https://chromestatus.com/feature/5172548013916160.

Most of the features of this API are represented in BCD already, but it was pointed out to me that SVG and MathML elements also take the global drawable attribute, so you can render SVG and MathML onto a canvas using HTML-in-Canvas.

This PR therefore adds data points for the drawable SVG and MathML global attributes.

I've also added data points for [HTML|SVG|MathML]Element.drawable, as I saw some evidence they exist, and logic suggests they should. However, on testing, they return undefined. I've asked the Chromium engineers for input on this (see mdn/content#46289 (comment)), as it seems like a bug to me.

I'll set this to draft status until I get an answer on this.

entry.title: Firefox relaxed referrer policies: partial from 100, not removed in 92
entry.content:
Firefox ignores the no-referrer-when-downgrade, origin-when-cross-origin and unsafe-url referrer policies for cross-site requests, and uses the default policy instead. This was added in https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1720294 and enabled by default in Firefox 100 in https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1761826.

The current data marks these values as removed in Firefox 92. This changes them to a partial implementation from Firefox 100, for the referrerpolicy attribute of <a>, <area>, <iframe>, <img>, <link> and <script>, the matching referrerPolicy properties, and the Referrer-Policy HTTP header.

Claude states this, but I have not verified it:

  • 92-99 only ignored the values in Nightly and early Beta: the pref was @IS_EARLY_BETA_OR_EARLIER@ until https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1761826 set it to true.
  • Same-site requests still use the values, so they aren't removed.
  • Cross-site top-level navigations still use them outside private browsing (https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1734328, also Firefox 100), which matters for <a>, <area> and the header (which also covers links followed from the page).

The same fix for svg.elements.a is in #31151.

Again, this seems reasonable to me from the bugs, but I'm hoping maybe you have tests for this?

Related docs work can be tracked in mdn/content#46466

entry.title: FF161 SVG image, script and feImage referrerpolicy
entry.content:
FF161 adds support for the referrerpolicy attribute and referrerPolicy property on SVG <image>, <script> and <feImage> in https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=2079321

The collector added api.SVGScriptElement.referrerPolicy in #31035. This adds the remaining features:

  • api.SVGImageElement.referrerPolicy
  • api.SVGFEImageElement.referrerPolicy (non-standard: Filter Effects doesn't define referrerpolicy, see w3c/svgwg#1171)
  • svg.elements.image.referrerpolicy
  • svg.elements.script.referrerpolicy
  • svg.elements.feImage.referrerpolicy (non-standard)

Claude states this, but I have not verified it:

  • Chrome: 113 for svg.elements.image.referrerpolicy only. Chrome's image loader reads referrerpolicy from whatever element it loads for, which includes SVG <image>, since chromium/chromium@4971c867d974 (refs/heads/main@{#1112277}). Chrome has no SVGImageElement.referrerPolicy property. The test results in w3c/svgwg#1171 show Chrome applies the attribute on <image> but not <script> or <feImage>, and Safari applies it on none of them.
  • Firefox ignores no-referrer-when-downgrade, origin-when-cross-origin and unsafe-url for cross-site requests from Firefox 100 (https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1761826). This adds those subfeatures with Firefox as partial, and corrects the existing svg.elements.a data, which had them removed in 92.

Related docs work can be tracked in mdn/content#46466
